question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the parts of Indian constitution?
I. Part VIII is related with the Union territories.
II. Part IX is related with the Co-Operative Societies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part VIII of the Indian Constitution (Articles 239–242) deals with The Union Territories (संघ राज्य क्षेत्र), so Statement I is correct.

• Part IX (Articles 243–243O) deals with The Panchayats, not Co-operative Societies, so Statement II is wrong.

• Co-operative Societies are covered under Part IX-B (Articles 243ZH–243ZT), added by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Part IX-A (Articles 243P–243ZG) deals with The Municipalities.

• The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 added Part IX (Panchayats); the 74th Amendment Act, 1992 added Part IX-A (Municipalities).

• Union Territories are administered by the President through an Administrator/Lieutenant Governor.

NOTE

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, as Part IX relates to Panchayats, not Co-operative Societies.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, because Statement II is false.

• Neither I Nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, because Statement I is true.

question: In July 2025, Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said the Kaladan project between India and Myanmar will be operational by _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2027.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In July 2025, Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal announced that the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project (कलादान बहुविध पारगमन परिवहन परियोजना) would be operational by 2027.

• The project connects Kolkata (India) with Sittwe port in Myanmar by sea, then to Mizoram via river and road.

• It aims to provide an alternative connectivity route to India's North-East, reducing dependence on the Siliguri Corridor ('Chicken's Neck').

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The project was framework-agreed between India and Myanmar in 2008.

• It links the Kaladan river with Mizoram's Zorinpui and further to the National Highway network.

• Sittwe Port lies in Myanmar's Rakhine State.

NOTE

• 2026 (Option 2): Incorrect year for the announced operational deadline.

• 2028 (Option 3): Incorrect year for the announced operational deadline.

• 2029 (Option 4): Incorrect year for the announced operational deadline.

question: As of 31st July 2025, which of the following country is the part of East Asia Summit Process?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Australia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Australia is one of the 18 participating members of the East Asia Summit (पूर्वी एशिया शिखर सम्मेलन) process.

• The EAS comprises the 10 ASEAN member states plus 8 partners: India, China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, the USA and Russia.

• The EAS was established in 2005, with the first summit held in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India has been a founding member of the EAS since 2005.

• The USA and Russia joined the EAS in 2011.

• The EAS is a leaders-led forum for dialogue on strategic, political and economic issues in the Indo-Pacific.

NOTE

• UAE (Option 2): Not a member of the East Asia Summit process.

• Saudi Arabia (Option 3): Not a member of the East Asia Summit process.

• Brazil (Option 4): Not a member of the East Asia Summit process.

question: Which freedom fighter was also known as 'Badshah Khan' or 'Frontier Gandhi'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abdul Ghaffar Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (खान अब्दुल गफ्फार खान) was popularly known as 'Badshah Khan', 'Bacha Khan' and 'Frontier Gandhi'.

• He founded the Khudai Khidmatgar ('Servants of God', Red Shirts) movement in 1929 based on non-violence.

• A close associate of Mahatma Gandhi, he championed Hindu-Muslim unity and non-violent struggle in the North-West Frontier Province.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• In 1987, he became the first non-Indian to be awarded the Bharat Ratna.

• He opposed the Partition of India in 1947.

• He is buried in Jalalabad, Afghanistan, as per his wish.

NOTE

• Ashfaqulla Khan (Option 2): Revolutionary of the Kakori Conspiracy (1925), hanged in 1927.

• Zakir Husain Khan (Option 3): The third President of India (1967–1969).

• Hakim Ajmal Khan (Option 4): Physician and freedom fighter, a founder of Jamia Millia Islamia.

question: Who has been appointed as the Director of the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) in December 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cherukumalli Srinivasa Rao.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Cherukumalli Srinivasa Rao (चेरुकुमल्ली श्रीनिवास राव) was appointed the Director of the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), Pusa, New Delhi in December 2024.

• IARI is India's premier national institute for agricultural research, education and extension, popularly known as Pusa Institute (पूसा संस्थान).

• It played a central role in India's Green Revolution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• IARI functions under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR).

• It was established in 1905 at Pusa, Bihar, and shifted to New Delhi in 1936.

• IARI awards post-graduate degrees as a deemed university.

NOTE

• Ajit Vinayak Gupte (Option 2): An Indian diplomat, not associated with IARI directorship.

• Pranay Verma (Option 3): Indian diplomat; India's High Commissioner to Bangladesh.

• Praveen Vashista (Option 4): Not the appointed Director of IARI.

question: There are _______ sub-schemes under the PM –YASASVI Scheme
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• There are 5 sub-schemes under the PM-YASASVI Scheme (पी.एम. यशस्वी योजना) — PM Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India.

• The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for OBC, EBC and DNT students.

• The five components are: Pre-Matric Scholarship, Post-Matric Scholarship, Top Class School Education, Top Class College Education, and Construction of Hostels.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• PM-YASASVI targets students from Other Backward Classes, Economically Backward Classes and De-notified Tribes.

• It merges several earlier scholarship and hostel programmes into a single umbrella scheme.

• Selection for the top-class components is through the YASASVI Entrance Test (YET) conducted by NTA.

NOTE

• 2 (Option 1): Incorrect number of sub-schemes.

• 7 (Option 3): Incorrect number of sub-schemes.

• 8 (Option 4): Incorrect number of sub-schemes.

question: Which ministry is the nodal ministry for the Bio-RIDE Scheme approved in September 2024?
option_3: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Science & Technology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ministry of Science & Technology (विज्ञान एवं प्रौद्योगिकी मंत्रालय) is the nodal ministry for the Bio-RIDE Scheme, approved by the Union Cabinet in September 2024.

• The scheme is implemented by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT) under this ministry.

• 'Bio-RIDE' stands for Biotechnology Research Innovation and Entrepreneurship Development.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The scheme merges the Biotechnology Research and Development and Industrial and Entrepreneurship Development (BIRAC) components.

• It aims to promote a Bio-Economy and support bio-entrepreneurs and startups.

• It aligns with India's 'BioE3' (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment) policy.

NOTE

• Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (Option 2): Handles public health and medical education, not the Bio-RIDE scheme.

• Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (Option 3): Deals with renewable energy sources like solar and wind.

• Ministry of Education (Option 4): Handles school and higher education policy.

question: Who was the head coach of the team that won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rahul Dravid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rahul Dravid (राहुल द्रविड़) was the head coach of the Indian team that won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024.

• India defeated South Africa by 7 runs in the final held at Barbados to win the title.

• It was India's second T20 World Cup title, after 2007.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Rohit Sharma was the captain of the winning Indian team.

• Virat Kohli was named Player of the Match in the final; Jasprit Bumrah was Player of the Tournament.

• The 2024 edition was co-hosted by the West Indies and the USA.

NOTE

• Jonathan Trott (Option 1): Head coach of Afghanistan's cricket team.

• Andrew McDonald (Option 2): Head coach of the Australian cricket team.

• Rob Walter (Option 4): Was the head coach of South Africa (the runner-up).

question: Volleyball made its Olympic debut at the _____ Olympic games.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1964.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Volleyball (वॉलीबॉल) made its Olympic debut at the 1964 Summer Olympic Games held in Tokyo, Japan.

• Both men's and women's volleyball were introduced at the same Games.

• The Soviet Union won the men's title and Japan won the women's title in 1964.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Volleyball was invented in 1895 by William G. Morgan in the USA.

• Beach volleyball was added to the Olympic programme later, at the 1996 Atlanta Games.

• The international governing body for volleyball is the FIVB.

NOTE

• 1958 (Option 1): Not an Olympic year; incorrect.

• 1960 (Option 2): Rome Olympics, but volleyball was not yet included.

• 1962 (Option 3): Not an Olympic year; incorrect.

question: In 2025, hockey Men's Asia Cup was held in which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 2025 Men's Hockey Asia Cup (पुरुष हॉकी एशिया कप) was held in India, at Rajgir in Bihar.

• India won the title by defeating South Korea in the final.

• The victory also secured India a direct berth for the 2026 FIH World Cup.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Men's Hockey Asia Cup is organised by the Asian Hockey Federation.

• The tournament was first held in 1982.

• India is the most successful team in the history of the Men's Hockey Asia Cup.

NOTE

• Sri Lanka (Option 2): Did not host the 2025 Men's Hockey Asia Cup.

• China (Option 3): Did not host the 2025 Men's Hockey Asia Cup.

• Bangladesh (Option 4): Did not host the 2025 Men's Hockey Asia Cup.

question: Who among the following is a violinist hailed from Andhra Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dwaram Venkataswamy Naidu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dwaram Venkataswamy Naidu (द्वारम वेंकटस्वामी नायडू) was a legendary Carnatic violinist (वायलिन वादक) from Andhra Pradesh.

• He was known for his mastery of the violin as a solo instrument in Carnatic music.

• He was awarded the Padma Shri in 1957.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He served as the Principal of the Maharaja's Government College of Music, Vizianagaram.

• He received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contribution to Carnatic music.

• The Government of Andhra Pradesh instituted awards in his memory.

NOTE

• U. Srinivas (Option 1): Famous mandolin (Carnatic mandolin) player from Andhra Pradesh.

• Chitti Babu (Option 2): Renowned Carnatic veena player.

• Sheik Chinna Moulana (Option 3): Celebrated nadaswaram player.

question: Who is the author of the book 'The God of Small Things'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arundhati Roy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Arundhati Roy (अरुंधति रॉय) is the author of the novel 'The God of Small Things' (द गॉड ऑफ स्मॉल थिंग्स).

• The novel was published in 1997 and won the Booker Prize the same year.

• It was her debut novel and is set in Kerala.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• She became the first Indian woman to win the Booker Prize.

• Her second novel is 'The Ministry of Utmost Happiness' (2017).

• She is also known for her political activism and non-fiction essays.

NOTE

• Ruskin Bond (Option 1): Author of 'The Room on the Roof', 'A Flight of Pigeons'.

• R.K. Narayan (Option 3): Author of 'Malgudi Days', 'The Guide', 'Swami and Friends'.

• Mulk Raj Anand (Option 4): Author of 'Untouchable' and 'Coolie'.

question: Natya Shastra by Bharat Muni clubbed musical instruments into how many groups?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Natya Shastra (नाट्य शास्त्र) by Bharata Muni, musical instruments are classified into 4 groups.

• The four categories are Tata (stringed), Avanaddha (percussion/membrane), Ghana (solid/idiophones) and Sushira (wind) instruments.

• This ancient classification is still the basis of Indian instrument categorisation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Tata Vadya are stringed instruments like the veena and sitar.

• Avanaddha Vadya are covered instruments like the tabla and mridangam.

• Sushira Vadya are wind instruments like the flute and shehnai; Ghana Vadya are solid instruments like cymbals.

NOTE

• 2 (Option 1): Incorrect number of instrument groups.

• 3 (Option 2): Incorrect number of instrument groups.

• 5 (Option 4): Incorrect number of instrument groups.

question: Who is the author of the book 'Miss Laila, Armed and Dangerous'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manu Joseph.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Manu Joseph (मनु जोसेफ) is the author of the novel 'Miss Laila, Armed and Dangerous' (मिस लैला, आर्म्ड एंड डेंजरस).

• The book was published in 2017.

• Manu Joseph is an Indian journalist and novelist.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• His debut novel 'Serious Men' (2010) won the Hindu Literary Prize.

• 'Serious Men' was later adapted into a film on Netflix.

• His other works include 'The Illicit Happiness of Other People'.

NOTE

• Sachin Kundalkar (Option 1): Marathi filmmaker and writer, author of 'Cobalt Blue'.

• Ruchir Joshi (Option 2): Author of 'The Last Jet-Engine Laugh'.

• Ajay K Pandey (Option 4): Author of 'You Are the Best Wife' and other popular fiction.

question: Which of the following temples is also known as "Taj Mahal of the South"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meenakshi Temple, Madurai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Meenakshi Amman Temple, Madurai (मीनाक्षी मंदिर, मदुरै) is popularly referred to as the "Taj Mahal of the South".

• It is a historic Hindu temple located on the southern bank of the Vaigai River in Tamil Nadu.

• It is dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi (a form of Parvati) and her consort Sundareswarar (Shiva).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The temple is famous for its towering, colourful gopurams (gateway towers).

• It is a masterpiece of Dravidian temple architecture, largely rebuilt during the Nayaka rule.

• The temple's Hall of Thousand Pillars is a notable attraction.

NOTE

• Sri Jagannath Puri Temple, Puri (Option 1): A 12th-century temple in Odisha, one of the Char Dham.

• Sri Venkateswara Temple, Tirupati (Option 3): Famous Vishnu temple on Tirumala hills, Andhra Pradesh.

• Chamundeshwari Temple, Mysore (Option 4): Temple on Chamundi Hills, Karnataka, dedicated to Goddess Chamundeshwari.

question: 'Raja' festival is celebrated in which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 'Raja' festival (राजा त्योहार), also called Raja Parba, is celebrated in the state of Odisha.

• It is a three-day festival that celebrates womanhood and the onset of the monsoon.

• It also marks the belief that Mother Earth (Bhudevi) undergoes her menstruation cycle during these days.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The three days are named Pahili Raja, Raja (Mithuna Sankranti) and Bhu Daha (Basi Raja).

• Girls and women enjoy swings, wear new clothes and refrain from work during the festival.

• A special pancake called 'Poda Pitha' is prepared during the festival.

NOTE

• Nagaland (Option 1): Known for festivals like Hornbill and Sekrenyi, not Raja.

• Gujarat (Option 2): Known for Navratri, Uttarayan (Kite festival), not Raja.

• Karnataka (Option 3): Known for Mysore Dasara, Ugadi, not Raja.

question: In which Indian state is the 'Garia' dance traditionally performed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tripura.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 'Garia' dance (गरिया नृत्य) is traditionally performed in the state of Tripura.

• It is associated with the Garia Puja, performed by tribal communities for a good harvest and prosperity.

• The dance is linked to the worship of Lord Garia, a deity of livestock and wealth.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Tripura include Hojagiri, Lebang Boomani and Sangrai.

• The Garia festival is celebrated in the month of April.

• Tripura is predominantly inhabited by tribes such as the Tripuri and Reang.

NOTE

• Gujarat (Option 1): Known for Garba and Dandiya Raas dances.

• Jharkhand (Option 2): Known for Chhau, Paika and Jhumar dances.

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Known for Lavani and Tamasha dances.

question: What is the name of the long-range glide bomb successfully tested by DRDO from a Su-30 MKI aircraft in 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gaurav.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gaurav (गौरव) is the long-range glide bomb successfully test-fired by the DRDO from a Su-30 MKI aircraft.

• It is an air-launched, long-range Glide Bomb (ग्लाइड बम) capable of hitting targets around 100 km away.

• It was developed indigenously by DRDO's Research Centre Imarat (RCI), Hyderabad.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Gaurav uses a hybrid navigation system with INS and GPS for precision.

• A lighter variant of the glide bomb is called 'Gautham'.

• Being a glide bomb, it has no propulsion and glides to its target after release.

NOTE

• Prithvi (Option 1): A surface-to-surface short-range ballistic missile, not a glide bomb.

• Agni (Option 2): A family of medium to intercontinental range ballistic missiles.

• BrahMos (Option 4): A supersonic cruise missile developed jointly by India and Russia.

question: What was the primary cause of India's 1991 economic crisis?
option_2: The government inability to repay foreign borrowings.
option_3: The state government inefficiency to not contribute to national economy.
option_4: High level of illegal migration from Pakistan and Bangladesh.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The government inability to repay foreign borrowings..

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The primary cause of India's 1991 economic crisis (1991 का आर्थिक संकट) was the government's inability to repay its foreign borrowings, i.e. a Balance of Payments (भुगतान संतुलन) crisis.

• India's foreign exchange reserves had dropped to a level sufficient for only about two to three weeks of imports.

• India had to pledge its gold reserves to raise emergency foreign exchange.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The crisis led to the New Economic Policy of 1991 (Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation - LPG reforms).

• Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister and P. V. Narasimha Rao was the Prime Minister at the time.

• The Gulf War of 1990–91 worsened the crisis by raising oil prices and cutting remittances.

NOTE

• A major natural disaster (Option 1): Not the cause; the crisis was a fiscal and balance of payments problem.

• The state government inefficiency... (Option 3): Not the primary cause of the 1991 crisis.

• High level of illegal migration... (Option 4): Unrelated to the balance of payments crisis.

question: In India, Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) was incepted in the year _____
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1991.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) (विदेश व्यापार महानिदेशालय) was set up in India in the year 1991.

• It is an attached office of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

• Earlier it was known as the Chief Controller of Imports & Exports (CCI&E).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• DGFT is responsible for formulating and implementing the Foreign Trade Policy (FTP).

• It issues the Importer Exporter Code (IEC), mandatory for import/export.

• Its headquarters is located in New Delhi.

NOTE

• 1997 (Option 1): Incorrect year of inception of DGFT.

• 1995 (Option 3): Incorrect year of inception of DGFT.

• 1993 (Option 4): Incorrect year of inception of DGFT.

question: Which of the following veto powers is not available to the President of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Qualified Veto.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Qualified Veto (विशेषित वीटो) is NOT available to the President of India.

• A qualified veto is one that can be overridden by the legislature with a higher (special) majority; it is exercised by the US President, not the Indian President.

• The President of India possesses the Absolute Veto, Suspensive Veto and Pocket Veto.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Absolute Veto: withholding assent to a bill so that it does not become law.

• Suspensive Veto: returning a bill (other than a money bill) for reconsideration, which Parliament can override by an ordinary majority.

• Pocket Veto: the President neither gives assent nor returns the bill, keeping it pending indefinitely.

NOTE

• Absolute Veto (Option 1): Available to the Indian President; the bill is completely rejected.

• Pocket Veto (Option 2): Available; famously used by President Zail Singh on the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill.

• Suspensive Veto (Option 4): Available; the President can return a bill for reconsideration.

question: Who decides whether a bill is a Money Bill or not?
option_2: Speaker of the House of the People
solution_text:
The correct answer is Speaker of the House of the People.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Speaker of the House of the People (Lok Sabha) (लोकसभा अध्यक्ष) decides whether a bill is a Money Bill or not.

• This power is provided under Article 110 of the Indian Constitution.

• The Speaker's decision on this matter is final and cannot be questioned in any court.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and only on the recommendation of the President.

• The Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations on a Money Bill, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.

• The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within 14 days.

NOTE

• President (Option 1): Gives recommendation for introduction and assent, but does not certify a bill as a Money Bill.

• Prime Minister (Option 3): Head of government, has no constitutional role in certifying Money Bills.

• Finance Minister (Option 4): Presents the budget but does not decide whether a bill is a Money Bill.

question: Carbon dioxide is transported to the lungs from all parts of the body through _____ in humans.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Blood.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In humans, carbon dioxide is transported from all parts of the body to the lungs through the Blood (रुधिर).

• CO2 is carried mainly as bicarbonate ions (about 70%) in the blood plasma.

• Some CO2 is carried bound to haemoglobin (as carbaminohaemoglobin) and a small part dissolved in plasma.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• At the lungs, CO2 is released from the blood and exhaled out during breathing.

• Oxygen is transported from the lungs to tissues mainly bound to haemoglobin (as oxyhaemoglobin).

• The exchange of gases at the alveoli and tissues occurs by diffusion.

NOTE

• Sweat (Option 1): Excretes water and salts through skin; not a CO2 transport medium.

• Mucus (Option 2): Traps dust and microbes in the respiratory tract; not a CO2 carrier.

• Lymph (Option 4): Carries fats and immune cells; not the primary carrier of CO2 to the lungs.

question: Mahavira Jain was born in a royal family near which ancient city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vaishali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism, was born in a royal family at Kundagrama (Kundalpur) near the ancient city of Vaishali (वैशाली) in present-day Bihar.

• He was born around 599 BCE into the Kshatriya Jnatrika clan.

• His father was Siddhartha and his mother was Trishala.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Mahavira attained Kaivalya (omniscience) and preached the five vows: Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Brahmacharya and Aparigraha.

• He attained nirvana at Pavapuri.

• Vaishali was the capital of the Vajji/Lichchhavi confederacy, one of the earliest republics.

NOTE

• Taxila (Option 1): An ancient centre of learning in the north-west (present-day Pakistan).

• Ujjain (Option 3): Ancient city in Madhya Pradesh, capital of the Avanti Mahajanapada.

• Pataliputra (Option 4): Ancient capital of Magadha (present-day Patna).

question:
In initial filtrate of kidney, which of the following substance is selectively re-absorbed as the urine flows along the tube in a human kidney?
I. Glucose
II. Amino acids
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the human kidney, both Glucose (ग्लूकोज) and Amino acids (अमीनो अम्ल) are selectively re-absorbed from the initial filtrate as it flows along the renal tubule.

• This process is called selective reabsorption (चुनिंदा पुन: अवशोषण) and occurs mainly in the proximal convoluted tubule.

• Useful substances like glucose, amino acids, salts and much of the water are reabsorbed back into the blood.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The functional unit of the kidney is the nephron.

• Filtration occurs at the glomerulus (Bowman's capsule); reabsorption and secretion refine the filtrate into urine.

• Substances like urea and excess salts are largely retained in the filtrate and excreted as urine.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, as amino acids are also reabsorbed, not just glucose.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, as glucose is also reabsorbed, not just amino acids.

• Neither I nor I (Option 4): Incorrect, as both glucose and amino acids are reabsorbed.
